Fixed. The bead was right, and the hole was wider than "defense-in-depth": it was revocation suppression.

The check cert.issuer == CRL.issuer was gated on crl_issuer_cert.is_none(), and discovery always stores a signer, so discovery mode skipped it outright. Neither neighbouring check covers it: (2a) ties the CRL issuer to the DISCOVERED signer subject, which discovery satisfies by construction; (2b) ties the issuer argument to cert.issuer, which says nothing about the CRL. So the certificate and the CRL were never compared to each other.

Consequence: a direct CRL from an unrelated CA governed an unrelated certificate whenever that CRL signer was in the bundle. Such a CRL does not list the target serial, so check_revocation returned Ok(()) -- NOT REVOKED. Reaching it only requires influencing which CRL bytes are supplied, which is what fetching a CDP does.

Fix: enforce when crl_issuer_cert.is_none() OR (signer_discovered AND the CRL does not declare indirectCRL). Gating on the IDP flag preserves the RFC 5280 4.14.22-26 indirect cases where the DNs differ by design.

The old comment claimed discovery could be exempt because the 4.5 key-rollover case satisfies the test anyway (same issuer DN, different signing key). True -- and that is why the exemption bought nothing: it skipped the check precisely where it would have passed, while surrendering the case where the DNs genuinely disagree.

Also fixed in check_revocation_against_anchor, which lacked the check entirely. Without discovery its (2a)+(2b) imply it (both reduce to the anchor subject); under discovery they do not.

Tests in pkix-revocation/tests/crl_signer_revocation.rs:
- discovery_rejects_a_direct_crl_from_a_different_ca_than_the_certs_issuer (GoodCA-issued EE vs TrustAnchorRootCRL; both legitimate, only the pairing wrong)
- discovery_accepts_a_direct_crl_from_the_certs_own_issuer (so a check rejecting every discovered direct CRL would not pass)

Verified by reverting the condition: the negative test then fails with Ok(()) instead of CrlIssuerMismatch. Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, 2342 tests.
